known_before_this_followup: Across the full resource-eligible panel, resolved host-species count is strongly associated with effective contributor number.
Host-family breadth is associated with contributor architecture but much less strongly than resolved host-species count.
One-family species can range from one resolved host species to dozens.

ecological_question: Within a fixed level of host-family breadth, does host-species richness still predict the architecture of anthropogenic geographic resource opportunity?

hypothesis.statement: Host-species richness within host-family strata increases portfolio-style anthropogenic opportunity, demonstrating that taxonomic family breadth and species-level resource breadth are distinct specialization dimensions.

primary_descriptive.association_1: Spearman(resolved host-species count, effective contributor number)
primary_descriptive.association_2: Spearman(resolved host-species count, maximum single-host fractional share)
primary_descriptive.reason: Host-family breadth is exactly constant at one family, so any association reflects species-level host portfolio variation within taxonomic specialists.

secondary_descriptive: Repeat both associations in 2-family, 3-5-family, and 6+ family strata.
Within each stratum, Spearman(resolved host-species count, introduced-added resource units).
Within each stratum, summarize median effective contributor number by tertile of resolved host-species richness.
